items.title: Discharge reconciliation by technicians is thinly described
items.whyItMatters: The committee's decision is about discharge, where only a few reports exist (claim c2).
items.opportunity: Search grey literature and professional organisations for discharge programmes.

items.title: Scope of practice differs by jurisdiction and changes over time
items.whyItMatters: What is allowed elsewhere may not be allowed here (claim c3).
items.opportunity: Chart the jurisdiction and date of every regulatory statement.

items.title: Outcome definitions are inconsistent
items.whyItMatters: Discrepancy counts cannot be compared across reports (claim c4).
items.opportunity: Chart each definition and the reference standard used.

items.title: Rural and weekend coverage
items.whyItMatters: Patients discharged at weekends or from rural sites are least likely to have a reconciled list.
items.opportunity: Chart setting, weekend coverage and supervision distance in every report.

items.title: Patient-reported outcomes are almost never measured
items.whyItMatters: Patients' understanding of their medicines after discharge is missing from the evidence.
items.opportunity: Record whether any patient-reported outcome was used.

errorsFound: The first scan reply assigned a moderate certainty although the recorded search returned no records, and it presented the search as confirmed empty.
reevaluation: The gaps confirm a scoping review that charts discharge programmes, supervision, regulatory scope with dates, outcome definitions and rural or weekend coverage.
summary: Five gaps: thin discharge evidence, jurisdiction-specific scope, inconsistent definitions, rural and weekend coverage, and missing patient outcomes.
